title: Electrochemical and hot corrosion behaviour of annealed AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating over steel.

recollection.starting_material: Steel substrate with AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating
recollection.intervention: Annealing process applied to the HEA coating
recollection.structure: Modified microstructure of the HEA coating, likely with improved phase distribution or grain refinement
recollection.mechanism: Annealing likely enhances diffusion and phase stability, improving corrosion resistance and mechanical properties
recollection.results: Improved electrochemical and hot corrosion resistance of the annealed HEA coating compared to the as-deposited state

score.note: The recollection identifies annealing of an AlCoCrFeNi coating and generically suggests grain refinement and improved corrosion behavior, but gives no annealing temperatures, coating method, phases, passive-layer mechanism, or numerical results. The proposed diffusion/phase-stability mechanism is vague and does not capture the reported role of BCC structure, grain refinement, sluggish diffusion, and Al/Cr-rich passive oxides.
